memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When Reuben heard this, he tried to rescue him from their hands. 'Let's not take his life,' he said. 'Don't shed any blood. Throw him into this cistern here in the wilderness, but don't lay a hand on him.' Reuben said this to rescue him from them and take him back to his father." - Gen 37:21-22 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Into the dark plot comes one dissenting voice. Reuben, the eldest, cannot bring himself to join in murder. "Let's not take his life," he pleads. He proposes they throw Joseph into a pit instead — secretly intending to come back later, rescue him, and return him safely to their father.

Reuben's courage was real, but imperfect. He did not boldly refuse the whole evil or stand openly against his brothers; he tried to steer them toward a lesser wrong and work behind the scenes. His plan was half-measures. Yet even so, his intervention spared Joseph's life at that crucial moment. Because Reuben spoke up, Joseph was not killed.

There is encouragement here for us. We may not always have the strength to stop every wrong or to make a perfect stand. But even a hesitant voice that says, "Let's not," can prevent great harm. God can use our imperfect courage.

When you find yourself among people rushing toward something wrong, will you be the one who speaks up, even weakly? Do not despise a small stand for good. Silence lets evil run its course, but a single voice of restraint — however imperfect — can make all the difference. God honours those who resist evil, even in the smallest way.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I willing to be a voice of restraint when others rush toward wrong?
2. Do I let imperfection keep me from making any stand at all?
3. Where might even a small "Let's not" prevent real harm?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, give me courage to speak up against wrong, even when my stand feels weak. Use my imperfect efforts to prevent harm, and keep me from silence when I should speak. Amen.
